messages:
maria: quick heads-up — onboarding a new int4 canary (raven-lite-int4). We're seeing ~0.8% structured-invoke schema failures vs the float baseline on the same prompt set. Dumped 30 failing examples, looks like 3 recurring patterns.

sam: can you paste one of the failing outputs? is it full parse error or schema mismatch? :eyes:

maria: sure — two representative types below. first is a malformed JSON (truncated/suffix noise):

maria: ```
{"action": "create_ticket", "metadata": {"severity": "low", "title": "Login issue"}, "notes": "user reported intermittent auth"}
# actually this one is fine — example 2 below (truncated streaming):
{"action": "create_ticket", "metadata": {"severity": "low", "title": "Expired token", "user": "u123"}, "extra": "some debug info"
```

maria: you'll notice example 2 is missing the final closing brace (likely stream cutoff / tokenization boundary).

miguel: interesting — do we see the truncated ones only on int4? any sign of tokenization changes vs float?

maria: yes — these truncations are present almost exclusively on the int4 canary. float32 baseline was clean on same requests. Also a smaller class of failures are valid JSON but missing required fields: e.g. action = null or metadata.title omitted.

tess: could be model distribution shift under quantization causing shorter tail completions or early EOS. Did you compare token-level EOS probability or avg length?

maria: we checked avg token length — int4 outputs are ~2 tokens shorter on average for this prompt family. EOS mass shifts look suspicious.

sam: two immediate mitigation ideas: 1) bump max tokens / force eos token handling, 2) adjust retry/rescue policy to include JSON wrapping heuristics.

miguel: for retries we currently do: 2 retries with simple json-wrap (prefix/suffix braces) + schema-validate. Proposal: make rescue policy multi-step and record which step fixed it:
- step A: json-wrap (prefix with '{' and suffix with '}')
- step B: run jsonlint-repair heuristic (balance braces, remove trailing garbage)
- step C: if still invalid, mark as parse_error and return structured fallback {"action":"undetermined","reason":"parse_error"}

sam: +1 for staged rescue and telemetry. We should also tag which model/config produced the error (quantization bits, kernel).

tess: for evaluation, we should add a small coverage benchmark: run 10k prompts across float/int variants and measure: parse_fail_rate, missing_required_field_rate, avg_tokens, and functional correctness (syntactic + semantic). Compare side-by-side and log diffs. I'll take that on.

maria: thanks. miguel can you run a targeted kv-prefix streaming test to see if prefix truncation correlates with batch sizes / kernel choices? maybe try batch_size=1 and continuous batching off.

miguel: will run. quick notes on where failures cluster: high-latency tails and when prefix contains long context (kvcache re-use). Could be kv-cache truncation causing stream boundary mid-json.

ci-bot: Canary job raven-lite-int4:run#202 deployed at 1778881200 — queued 1200 reqs, sampled 300 for structured-output eval. CI report posted: link: https://ci.internal/runs/202

sam: once we have the failing corpus, we should craft a small repair model/test harness: for each failed output run the repair heuristics and verify schema acceptance and semantic fidelity (no invented actions). If repair changes action, mark as "repaired-with-modification".

maria: filing INF-876 to track: include failing examples, rescue-step outcomes, and canary metrics. Owners: tess -> benchmark run and ground-truth eval, miguel -> kv-prefix and batch experiments, sam -> retry/rescue implementation + telemetry schema. I'll paste the sample corpus into the ticket.

tess: question — do we want to gate onboarding if parse_fail_rate > 0.5% for structured actions? current SLO is 0.1% but maybe relax for int4 initial brings and require explicit canary policy.

sam: keep SLO but allow a canary grace window with increased monitoring and auto-rollout block if >1% for 24h.

maria: agreed. I'll update the canary dashboard to show step-level rescue counts and a new metric `struct_parse_rescue_rate`.

miguel: I'll try batch_size=1 + disable continuous batching for the next canary run (on raven-lite-int4) and post results here. ETA 2h.

maria: thanks — let's reconvene after those runs. :thumbsup:
